Rashi on Chullin 17a:10:1.hebrew: כי אסר רחמנא - בשר תאוה במדבר:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:10:1.english: When the Merciful One prohibited - [He prohibited] meat of desire in the wilderness.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:11:1.hebrew: שהכניסו ישראל - אליבא דר' עקיבא מהו לאוכלן אחר כניסתן? מי אמרינן כי אסר רחמנא בשר נחירה לאחר ביאה, הני מילי לנחור אחרי כן לאכול, אבל הנחורות ובאות מן המדבר, הואיל ובשעת נחירתן היתר היתה, תו לא מתסרי? או דלמא לא שנא? ודרוש וקבל שכר, הוא שצריכין אנו לעמוד על האמת ואע"פ שכבר עבר:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:11:1.english: That Israel brought in - According to Rabbi Akiva, what is the law regarding eating them after their entry? Do we say that when the Merciful One prohibited the flesh of nehira after the entry [into the Land], this applies only to stabbing [an animal] afterward in order to eat it; but [animals] that were stabbed and are coming from the desert, since at the time of their stabbing it was permitted, they are no longer prohibited? Or perhaps there is no difference? And "expound and receive reward" [means] that we must arrive at the truth, even though [the time in question] has already passed:

Rashi on Chullin 17a:12:1.hebrew: ובתים מלאים כל טוב וגו' - סיפיה דקרא: "ואכלת ושבעת":
Rashi on Chullin 17a:12:1.english: "And houses full of all good things, etc." - The end of the verse: "And you shall eat and be satisfied."

Rashi on Chullin 17a:12:2.hebrew: כתלי דחזירי - חזירים יבשים, שקורין בקונ"ש:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:12:2.english: Dried pork [lit. "walls of pigs"] - Dried pigs, which are called in the vernacular "konesh."

Rashi on Chullin 17a:13:1.hebrew: אלא לאחר מכאן - דהיינו בשבע שחלקו, דלא שרא להו רחמנא טומאה אלא בשעת שלל, כדכתיב (דברים כ) ואכלת את שלל אויביך וגו'. שבע שנים כבשו ושבע שנים חלקו, כדאמרי' בפרק אין נערכין (ערכין דף יב:):
Rashi on Chullin 17a:13:1.english: Rather, after this - That is, in the seven years of division, for the Merciful One permitted them [to eat] impure [food] only at the time of the spoils, as it is written (Deuteronomy 20): "And you shall eat the spoil of your enemies," etc. They conquered for seven years and divided for seven years, as we say in the chapter "Ein Ne'erakhin" (Arakhin 12b):

Rashi on Chullin 17a:13:2.hebrew: שלל של עובדי כוכבים - כדכתיב (דברים ו) "אשר לא מלאת", וכתיב נמי "את שלל אויביך":
Rashi on Chullin 17a:13:2.english: The spoils of idolaters - As it is written (Deuteronomy 6): "[houses full of all good things] that you did not fill," and it is also written: "the spoil of your enemies."

Rashi on Chullin 17a:14:1.hebrew: שנית הכל שוחטין - ומוקמת לה בנשחטין, כדאמרן "הכל טעונים שחיטה, ואפי' עוף":
Rashi on Chullin 17a:14:1.english: The second [mishna]: "All may slaughter" - And it is established as referring to [animals] that are being slaughtered, as we said: "All require slaughter, even a bird."

Rashi on Chullin 17a:14:2.hebrew: ולעולם שוחטין - נמי מוקמת ליה כדאמרן, דאשמעינן דאע"פ שגלו לא חזרו להיתירן הראשון, ואין בשר נאכל אלא בשחיטה:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:14:2.english: And in fact, they slaughter - You also establish it [the mishna] as we said, that it teaches us that even though they went into exile, they did not return to their original permitted status, and meat may be eaten only through slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:15:1.hebrew: וכי תימא בין בצור כו' - דלאו בנשחטין אתא לאורויי, אלא בשוחטין:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:15:1.english: And if you say, "whether with a flint, etc." - [You might say that the word "all" in the mishna] does not come to teach about those who are slaughtered [i.e., which animals may be slaughtered], but rather about those who slaughter [i.e., who is fit to slaughter].

Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רבא - כולה בשוחטין והכל שוחטין תרתי דתני במתני':
Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:1.english: Rather, Rava said - The entire [mishna] is about "those who slaughter" and "everyone slaughters"; these are two [distinct statements] that [the Tanna] taught in the mishna:

Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:2.hebrew: חדא לכותי וחדא למומר - כדאמרן בריש פירקין (חולין דף ג.):
Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:2.english: One to include a Cuthean, and one to include an apostate - As we said at the beginning of the chapter (Chullin 3a).

Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:3.hebrew: בין בלילה - כשאבוקה כנגדו, כדאוקימנא (לעיל חולין דף יג:):
Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:3.english: Whether at night - When a torch is opposite him, as we established (above, Chullin 13b).

Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:4.hebrew: בין בראש הגג - ולא חיישינן דלימרו לצבא השמים עולה לשחוט:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:4.english: Whether on the top of a roof - And we are not concerned that people will say, "He is slaughtering an offering to the host of heaven."

Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:5.hebrew: בין בראש הספינה - ואע"ג דתנן לקמן (חולין דף מא.) אין שוחטין לתוך ימים, בראש הספינה שרי, דמוכחא מילתא דלנקר ספינתו הוא צריך:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:16:5.english: Whether at the front of the ship - Even though we learned later (Chullin 41a) that one may not slaughter into the sea, at the front of the ship it is permitted, since it is evident that he needs [the blood] to clean out his ship.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:17:1.hebrew: פגם ושדר פגם ושדר - עשה בסכין פגימות הרבה שאינן דומות זו לזו, ושדר לא"י לידע איזו אסורה ואיזו כשרה. כן עשה פעמים ושלש:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:17:1.english: He nicked [the knife] and sent [it], nicked and sent - He made many nicks in a knife that were not similar to one another, and sent [it] to the Land of Israel to find out which [nick] disqualifies [the slaughter] and which is valid. He did so two and three times.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:17:2.hebrew: שלחו ליה - סימן זה יהא לך בפגימות:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:17:2.english: They sent to him - This shall be a sign for you regarding nicks [in the knife]:

Rashi on Chullin 17a:17:3.hebrew: כמגירה שנינו - שפגימותיה מכוונות לעומקן, ויש לפגם שני עוקצים: כשאתה מוליך צפרנך מסוף הסכין לראשה, צפרנך חוגרת בעוקץ של צד הראש, וכשאתה בודק מראשה לסופה, צפרנך חוגרת בעוקץ של סופה:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:17:3.english: We learned it like a saw - Meaning, its notches are aligned with their depth, and the notch has two points: When you run your fingernail from the end of the knife to its head, your fingernail catches on the point at the head side, and when you check from its head to its end, your fingernail catches on the point at its end.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:1:1.english: And all the more so now - Since they were exiled [from the Land].

Rashi on Chullin 17a:2:1.hebrew: לאסור להם בשר נחירה - כדכתיב בההוא קרא דכי ירחק ממך המקום וגו', וזבחת מבקרך ומצאנך וגו':
Rashi on Chullin 17a:2:1.english: To prohibit them from [eating] meat of nechira - As it is written in that verse: "If the place... is too far from you..." etc., "then you shall slaughter from your herd and from your flock" etc.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:2:2.english: That at the beginning - In the wilderness.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:2:3.hebrew: הותר להם בשר נחירה - מהאי קרא נפקא ליה, דכתיב "כי ירחק" "וזבחת", מכלל דעד השתא לא נצטוו על הזביחה:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:2:3.english: Meat of nechirah was permitted to them - He derives this from this verse, as it is written: "When [the place] will be far... then you shall slaughter" (Deuteronomy 12:21). This implies that until now they were not commanded regarding slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:3:1.hebrew: ועכשיו שגלו - רב יוסף קאמר ליה:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:3:1.english: And now that they have been exiled - Rav Yosef said this [to the one who asked].

Rashi on Chullin 17a:4:1.hebrew: בשר תאוה לא איתסר כלל - וקרא, "ואל פתח אהל מועד לא הביאו" (ויקרא יז), בקדשים כתיב. והאי דכתיב (דברים יב) "בכל אות נפשך תאכל בשר", לאו לאורויי היתירא בבשר תאוה אתא, אלא כדדריש ליה רבי אלעזר בן עזריה בפרק כסוי הדם (לקמן חולין דף פד.): לימדה תורה דרך ארץ, שלא יאכל אדם בשר אלא לתיאבון. "וכי ירחק" "וזבחת", בא להזהיר על השחיטה כשיכנסו לארץ. ואע"ג דקרא בפסולי המוקדשין שנפדו על ידי מומין משתעי, כדמוקמינן בבכורות (דף לב.), אפילו הכי גמרינן חולין מינייהו, כדאמרינן בפ"ב (לקמן חולין דף כח.): מקיש צבי ואיל לפסולי המוקדשי' - מה פסולי המוקדשים בשחיטה, אף צבי ואיל בשחיטה, וצבי ואיל חולין נינהו:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:4:1.english: Meat of desire was not prohibited at all - And the verse says, "And to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting he has not brought it" (Leviticus 17); it is written regarding sacrificial animals. And as for that which is written (Deuteronomy 12), "In all the desire of your soul you may eat meat," it does not come to teach the permissibility of meat of desire, but rather as Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya expounds it in the chapter of Kisui HaDam (later, Chullin 84a): The Torah taught proper conduct, that a person should eat meat only out of appetite. And "when it is far" and "you shall slaughter" comes to warn about slaughter when they enter the Land. And even though the verse speaks of disqualified consecrated animals that were redeemed because of blemishes, as we establish in Bekhorot (page 32a), nevertheless we derive non-sacred animals from them, as we say in the second chapter (later, Chullin 28a): It juxtaposes the gazelle and the deer to disqualified consecrated animals - just as disqualified consecrated animals require slaughter, so too the gazelle and the deer require slaughter, and the gazelle and the deer are non-sacred animals.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:4:2.hebrew: בשר נחירה לא אישתרי כלל - הילכך לא תלה הכתוב בביאת הארץ אלא היתר בשר תאוה וזביחה. דכתיב בהאי קרא לאו בביאת הארץ נתלית, אלא אורחא דקרא למכתב זביחה באכילת בשר. אי נמי, למאי דדרשינן בבכורות (ד' טו.) "וזבחת ואכלת" - אין בפסולי המוקדשין שנפדו אלא היתר זביחה ואכילה, ולא גיזה ועבודה. אי נמי, לאסור שחיטת חולין בעזרה, כדדרשינן ליה בקדושין (דף נז:) "כי ירחק" "וזבחת" - בריחוק מקום אתה זובח, ואי אתה זובח בקירוב מקום:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:4:2.english: Meat of nehirah was not permitted at all - Therefore the verse did not make [the permission of nehirah] dependent on entering the land, but only the permission of meat of desire and of slaughter. For [the verse] that is written here is not made dependent on entering the land; rather, it is the way of Scripture to write "slaughter" in connection with eating meat. Alternatively, according to what we derive in Bekhorot (15a) from "and you shall slaughter and eat" - that in the case of disqualified consecrated animals that were redeemed, there is only permission to slaughter and eat, but not to shear or to work [with them]. Alternatively, it is to prohibit the slaughter of unconsecrated animals in the Temple courtyard, as we derive it in Kiddushin (page 57b) from "if it is far" "and you shall slaughter": you may slaughter when the place is far, but you may not slaughter when the place is near.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:5:1.hebrew: ושחט - אלמא נצטוו על השחיטה באהל מועד שבמדבר:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:5:1.english: "And he shall slaughter" - Evidently, they were commanded regarding slaughter at the Tent of Meeting in the wilderness.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:1.hebrew: ונתנבלה - כגון על ידי פגימת סכין, או שהייה, או דרסה:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:1.english: And it became an unslaughtered carcass (nevelah) - For example, through a nick in the knife, or a delay [in the slaughter], or pressing [the knife while slaughtering].

Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:2.hebrew: והנוחר - מדעת. ולשון נחירה, שקורעה לאורכה מנחיריה ועד החזה:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:2.english: And one who nochar - Knowingly. And the term *nechira* [means] that he tears it lengthwise, from its nostrils to the chest.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:3.hebrew: והמעקר - סימנין. ובחיה קאי, דטעונה כסוי, כגון צבי ואיל:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:3.english: And one who uproots - [The two] signs [of the windpipe and gullet]. And it refers to a wild animal (chayah) that requires covering [of its blood], such as a deer or a hart.

Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:4.hebrew: פטור מלכסות - דכתיב "אשר יאכל" "ושפך וכסה", בראוי לאכילה הכתוב מדבר. ואפילו מאן דמחייב כסוי בשוחט ונמצאת טרפה, הכא מודה דשחיטה מיהא בעינן, דגמר "שפיכה" "שפיכה" משחוטי חוץ, והתם שחיטה כתיב, בפרק כסוי הדם (לקמן חולין דף פה.):
Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:4.english: Exempt from covering - For it is written, "which may be eaten" (Leviticus 17:13), and "he shall pour out its blood and cover it"; the verse speaks of that which is fit to be eaten. And even the one who obligates covering when one slaughters an animal that is then found to be a *tereifa*, here he agrees that we require slaughter at least, since [the Gemara] derives "pouring" from "pouring" from those slaughtered outside [the Temple courtyard], and there slaughter is written. [This is discussed] in the chapter of Kisui HaDam (later, Chullin 85a).

Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:5.hebrew: אלא לר' עקיבא - על כסוי הדם במדבר נצטוו, ונחירתן היתה שחיטתן, והנוחר בזמן הזה נמי נבעי כסוי:
Rashi on Chullin 17a:7:5.english: But according to Rabbi Akiva - They were commanded about covering the blood in the wilderness, and their nechira was their slaughter, and one who performs nechira nowadays too would require covering [the blood].

Tosafot on Chullin 17a:13:1.hebrew: כי אישתרי שלל של עובדי כוכבים דידהו לא אישתרי - לא גרסינן. או דלמא לא שנא, דהלשון היה משמע שהיה מסתפק אי אישתרי כתלי דחזירי דידהו אי לא, וזה אינו; דמתחלה לא נסתפק מכתלי דחזירי דידהו, או במה שנחרו כשבאו, אלא במה שנחרו במדבר בהיתר. והש"ס הקשה לו דאפי' דבר טמא אשתרי להו, כלומר דאפילו לנחור בתחלה הם מותרים, כל שכן מה שנחרו קודם. ומשני דלמא שלל של עובדי כוכבים אישתרי להו ולא דידהו, ולכך אסור לנחור, והשתא שפיר מיבעיא לן במה שנחרו בהיתר:
Tosafot on Chullin 17a:13:1.english: "When the spoil of the idolaters was permitted, theirs was not permitted" - We do not have this text. "Or perhaps it makes no difference": for the wording would imply that he was in doubt whether the kitlei de-chazirei ("the kitlei of swine") of theirs were permitted or not, and this is not so; for initially he was not in doubt about the kitlei de-chazirei of theirs, nor about what they slaughtered by nechirah when they arrived, but rather about what they slaughtered by nechirah in the wilderness, with permission. And the Gemara challenged him: even a forbidden thing was permitted to them, meaning that even to perform nechirah initially they were permitted, all the more so what they had performed nechirah on earlier. And it answers: perhaps the spoil of the idolaters was permitted to them, but not [the animals] of theirs, and therefore it is forbidden to perform nechirah, and now it is well that we ask about what they performed nechirah on with permission.

Tosafot on Chullin 17a:1:1.hebrew: וכל שכן השתא דארחיקו להו טובא - לספרים דגרסי "באלו הן הלוקין" (מכות דף יט.) "לעולם לא קידשה לעתיד לבא", אם כן לר' ישמעאל הותרו הבמות. וקשה, דאם כן מאי קאמר הכא לר' ישמעאל דארחיקו להו טפי? אדרבה, אקריבו להו טפי כיון דהותרו הבמות:
Tosafot on Chullin 17a:1:1.english: And all the more so now that they were distanced greatly - According to the versions that read in [the chapter] "These are the ones who receive lashes" (Makkot 19a): "[The Temple site] never became sanctified for the future to come," if so, according to R. Yishmael the private altars (bamot) were permitted. And it is difficult: if so, what does it say here, according to R. Yishmael, that they were distanced further? On the contrary, they should have offered more, since the bamot were permitted!

Tosafot on Chullin 17a:4:1.hebrew: רבי עקיבא סבר בשר תאוה לא איתסר כלל - תימה, מנא ליה הא? דלמא מר אמר חדא ומר אמר חדא, ולא פליגי? וי"ל, אי לרבי עקיבא מיתסר בשר תאוה, אם כן היכי הותרה להם בשר נחירה? דבקדשים מודה דבעיא שחיטה, כדמשמע בסמוך; ואי בצבי ואיל, הא בקרא דדרשינן מיניה היתר נחירה כתיב בקר וצאן, כדכתיב כי ירחק ממך וזבחת מבקרך ומצאנך, מכלל דמעיקרא לא בעו זביחה. ומיהו קשה, דהוה ליה לאוקומי קרא דהיתר נחירה בבעלי מומין דלא חזו להקרבה:
Tosafot on Chullin 17a:4:1.english: Rabbi Akiva holds that the meat of desire was not prohibited at all - It is astonishing: from where does he know this? Perhaps one Sage said one thing and the other Sage said another, and they do not disagree? And one can answer: if, according to Rabbi Akiva, the meat of desire was prohibited, then how was nechirah-meat permitted to them? For with regard to sacrifices, he agrees that slaughter is required, as is implied shortly below. And if [it was permitted] with regard to deer and ayal, behold, in the verse from which we derive the permission of nechirah, "cattle and flock" is written, as it is written, "If the place... is too far from you... then you shall slaughter of your cattle and of your flock" — implying that originally they did not require slaughter (zeviḥah). But nevertheless, it is difficult, for [the Gemara] should have established the verse permitting nechirah as referring to blemished animals, which are not fit for sacrifice:
